facts.text: Iran's parliamentary national-security committee approved a bill to charge rial-denominated transit fees on ships using the Strait of Hormuz, ban US and Israeli vessels and ships of countries applying sanctions on Iran, and draft the legal framework with Oman (CCTV via Odaily).

WSJ (via Odaily/PAP): Trump told aides he is willing to end the US military campaign against Iran even if Hormuz stays largely closed, settling for weakening Iran's navy and missile stocks and leaving the reopening for later; aides judged forcing the strait open would stretch the war beyond his 4-6 week timeline.

10Y closes 30 Mar (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 3.04%, OAT 3.77%, BTP 3.99%, Bonos 3.56%, gilt 4.94% -> OAT-Bund 73bp, BTP-Bund 95bp, Spain 52bp; Schatz 2.62%, gilt 2Y 4.45%; CZ2 4.29%, CZ10 4.97%, HU10 7.28%. Live 06:42: UST10 4.32%, UST2 3.81%, JGB10 2.34%.

31 Mar morning (Asia): MSCI Asia-Pacific heading for its worst month since October 2008; China's official manufacturing PMI 50.4 (50.1 expected, first expansion this year), services 50.1; EUR/USD 1.1470, USD/JPY 159.64, UST10 4.32% (-3bp), gold $4,564 (+1.2%). White House spokeswoman Leavitt said Trump may ask Gulf Arab states to help finance the war and that talks with Iran were going 'well'.

Other European data 31 Mar: German retail sales fell 0.6% m/m in February (+0.3% expected); German unemployment rate 6.3% as expected; UK Q4 GDP confirmed at +0.1% q/q (1.0% y/y), UK Q4 current-account deficit GBP18.4bn (2.4% of GDP); French household consumption -1.4% m/m in February (-0.3% expected).

TE (31 Mar): the Bund 10Y is ending March near 3.0% (close to its highest since May 2011) after a ~36-37bp monthly rise, the biggest since late 2022; OAT 10Y ~3.75% (highest since June 2009, +~50bp in March); BTP 10Y ~3.9-4.0% (+60-70bp in March); gilt 10Y ~4.85% (near highest since July 2008, +60bp). Yields eased during the day on growth worries.

TE (31 Mar): markets price at least two BoE hikes in 2026 with about a 50% chance of a move in April, a reversal from pre-war bets on two cuts; MPC member Alan Taylor (last week) set a 'high bar' for hikes and favoured steady rates until the war's impact is clearer. Sterling lost ~2% vs the dollar in March (~$1.32).

Euro-area flash HICP for March: 2.5% y/y (2.6% expected; February 1.9%), the highest since January 2025; core (ex energy, food, alcohol & tobacco) 2.3% (2.4% in February); services 3.2% (3.4%), energy +4.9% y/y (-3.1%) and +6.8% m/m. National HICP flashes: Germany 2.8% (2.0%), Spain 3.3% (2.5%), France 1.9% (1.1%), Italy 1.5% (unchanged), Netherlands 2.6%.

TE (31 Mar): Brent heads for a nearly 50% monthly gain (record), trading ~$107 (TE's quote, apparently the June contract; PAP's expiring May contract traded $116-119) after Iran hit the Kuwaiti tanker Al-Salmi near Dubai; gold tops $4,570 but heads for its worst month since 2008, silver its worst since 2011; the dollar heads for its best month since July 2025; UST10 4.30%, retreating from an eight-month high of 4.44% two sessions earlier (+~40bp in March).

31 Mar ~14:35: Brent May (expiring contract) +3.3% to $116.50, WTI May $103.10; UST10 4.31% (-3bp), 2s10s +51bp; Bund 10Y 3.02% (-2bp); DXY 100.27, EUR/USD 1.1497; gold $4,580, silver $73.69. S&P 500 and Dow head for their worst month since September 2022; oil heads for a record monthly gain.

TE (31 Mar, after the HICP flash): markets have abandoned earlier expectations of a ~40% chance of an ECB cut and now price at least two ECB hikes in 2026; Villeroy reaffirmed the ECB's resolve against energy-driven inflation but called discussion of the timing of any move premature. PAP (Reuters) likewise: investors price two ECB hikes by end-2026.

US data 31 Mar: JOLTS job openings 6.882m in February (6.89-6.92m expected; January revised 7.24m), quits 2.97m (lowest since Aug 2020); Conference Board consumer confidence 91.8 in March (87.8 expected); Case-Shiller 20-city +1.2% y/y in January (1.4% expected). Wall Street closed sharply higher (S&P 500 +2.9%, Nasdaq +3.8%) on hopes of an end to the war, but the S&P 500 lost more than 6% in March (worst month since Sept 2022) and ~6% in Q1.

TE (31 Mar): Lagarde and Lane outlined that the energy-shock developments are likely to warrant a hawkish ECB response, with the magnitude depending on the size of the shock; euro-area headline and core HICP came in slightly below expectations.

31 Mar European close (~18:00): UST10 4.33% (-2bp), 2s10s +51bp; Bund 10Y 3.01% (-1bp); DXY 100.17 (-0.3%), EUR/USD 1.1515 (ECB fix 1.1498), USD/JPY 159.08; Brent May (expiry) $118.90 (+5.4%), WTI $104.40; TTF EUR50/MWh (-9%; TE: still up >60% in March, the biggest monthly rise since Sept 2021); gold $4,620 (+2.1%), silver $73.8. STOXX 600 -6.5% in March, its worst month since June 2022.

Iranian President Pezeshkian (18:41): Iran is ready to end the war but wants guarantees; earlier the IRGC said US companies in the region become targets from 1 April. The Dow briefly rose more than 1,100 points on the report. China and Pakistan proposed a five-point initiative to restore peace in the Gulf.

PAP digest 31 Mar: Rubio (Al Jazeera) confirmed talks with Iran via intermediaries and said the US will reach its goals in 'weeks, not months' and Hormuz will be opened 'one way or another'; Trump (NY Post): countries that use Hormuz should unblock it, it will 'open automatically' once the US ends its operation; Hegseth: the coming days will be decisive. EU energy commissioner Jorgensen warned the crisis will not be short-lived (diesel and jet fuel constraints); US gasoline topped $4/gal for the first time since 2022 (AAA).

Schmid (Kansas City Fed, Tuesday): one should not assume higher energy prices only affect inflation temporarily, since inflation was near 3% before the war and progress to 2% has stalled; 'we cannot take risks to inflation expectations lightly' and policy must act to validate them. Jin10 notes markets had moved last week towards a possible hike later this year, but this week back towards a hold.

White House officials are assessing scenarios of oil at $150/bbl or higher (not ruling out $200) and considering extra emergency powers to curb fuel costs; Treasury's baseline is oil above $100 for some time (Odaily, 1 Apr 03:03). The CFTC said it is monitoring unusual trading in crude futures.

1 Apr early: Rubio said the US can 'see the finish line' of the Iran war; the WSJ reported the UAE is preparing to help the US open Hormuz by force (no Arab state has joined the war so far); Trump announced a prime-time address on Iran for 1 Apr 21:00 ET (03:00 Warsaw on 2 Apr) and told Reuters he is considering pulling the US out of NATO.

10Y closes 31 Mar: Bund 3.00%, OAT 3.72%, BTP 3.91%, Bonos 3.51%, gilt 4.92% -> OAT-Bund 72bp, BTP-Bund 91bp, Spain 51bp; Schatz 2.62%, gilt 2Y 4.41%; CZ2 4.28%, CZ10 4.93%, HU10 7.17%. Live 06:33: UST10 4.29%, UST2 3.77%, JGB10 2.32%.
Goldman Sachs (Jin10, 1 Apr): despite volatile fed-funds pricing since the war began, the likelihood of a Fed hike this year remains low; the Fed rarely tightens in response to oil shocks alone.
Czech manufacturing PMI jumped to 52.8 in March (50.0 expected; strongest since April 2022) with input prices rising at the fastest pace since October 2022; Hungary's HALPIM PMI fell to 50.4 (51.2).

Final March manufacturing PMIs (S&P Global): euro area 51.6 (flash 51.4; February 50.8; strongest since June 2022), Germany 52.2 (flash 51.7), France 50.0 (50.2); UK 51.0 (flash 51.4). Input-cost inflation hit its highest since late 2022 on oil, energy and chemicals.
TE (1 Apr): ECB pricing scaled back to two hikes by December, from three earlier in the week (before the war: no hikes, with a slight chance of easing). OAT 10Y ~3.6%, BTP ~3.8%.
TE (1 Apr): markets now price fewer than two BoE hikes in 2026, down from four in mid-March; gilt 10Y toward 4.75%; sterling recovered.
Euro-area unemployment rate rose to 6.2% in February (6.1% expected and the January record low).

1 Apr ~14:30: core bonds rallied on Trump's signals that the US could leave Iran 'in two or three weeks' with or without a deal: UST10 -4bp to 4.28% (back from the local high above 4.40%), Bund 10Y -6bp to 2.95%, gilt 10Y -9bp to 4.82%; Brent June briefly below $100 (-5.4% at the low), $101.2 at 14:27; DXY 99.4 (-0.4%); gold $4,786 (+2.3%).

Trump (1 Apr): the president of Iran's 'new regime' asked for a ceasefire, which he will consider when Hormuz is 'open, free and clear'; the US will withdraw 'soon' but without a timeline (operation to last 2-3 more weeks). Iran's FM Araghchi said he gets messages from Witkoff but these are not negotiations; Tehran denied requesting a ceasefire and the IRGC said Hormuz will not open. The WSJ reported Trump discussed leaving NATO if allies do not help open Hormuz.

Musalem (St. Louis Fed, AEI, 1 Apr): the 3.50-3.75% range is likely at the lower end of neutral and should remain appropriate for some time; he could back a cut if the labour market weakens or a hike if inflation rises or credibility slips; the energy shock will pass through one-for-one to headline and partly to core. Barkin (Richmond, Tuesday): firms still see high oil as a short-term disruption; the case for a hike would rest on rising inflation expectations, which he has not yet seen.

US data 1 Apr: ADP private payrolls +62k in March (40k expected; February revised to +66k); retail sales +0.6% m/m in February (0.5% expected; strongest in seven months); ISM manufacturing 52.7 (52.3-52.5 expected; February 52.4), the strongest since August 2022, with prices paid jumping to 78.3 (70.5), the highest since June 2022; S&P Global manufacturing PMI final 52.3.

1 Apr European close: UST10 4.30% (-1bp); Bund 10Y 2.99%; DXY 99.41 (-0.45%), EUR/USD 1.1611 (ECB fix 1.1605), USD/JPY 158.64; Brent June $101.79 (-2.1%), WTI May $99.81; TTF EUR47.7 (-5.9%); gold $4,778 (+2.8%; NY futures above $4,800), silver $75.9. Saudi oil exports fell ~50% in March (Odaily).

IEA's Birol (Reuters via PAP): supply disruptions from the Hormuz closure will be much more severe in April and will hit European countries; analysts see European gas at EUR80-120/MWh if Hormuz stays shut into winter.

Trump's prime-time address (2 Apr 03:00 Warsaw): the core strategic objectives are nearly achieved and the war is 'about to end', but the US will hit Iran 'extremely hard' over the next two-three weeks ('back to the Stone Age') and strike power plants and oil targets if no deal is reached; countries that use Hormuz should open it, and it will 'open naturally' after the conflict; he did not mention leaving NATO. Iran's military promised 'crushing' retaliation and fired missiles.

10Y closes 1 Apr: Bund 2.99%, OAT 3.67%, BTP 3.83%, Bonos 3.46%, gilt 4.83% -> OAT-Bund 68bp, BTP-Bund 84bp, Spain 47bp; Schatz 2.60%, gilt 2Y 4.30%; CZ2 4.18%, CZ10 4.86%, HU10 6.88%. Live 06:31 (after Trump's address): UST10 4.37% (4.32 prior), UST2 3.85%, JGB10 2.39%.
TE (2 Apr): with the Bund 10Y back above 3% (near the highest since May 2011), investors expect three ECB hikes in 2026, up from two a day earlier; BTP above 3.9%, OAT above 3.7%.

TE (2 Apr): investors again price two BoE hikes in 2026, reversing four days of reduced bets, despite Governor Bailey's recent warning that markets overestimate the likelihood of hikes; gilt 10Y back at 4.8%.

2 Apr ~14:00 after the address: Brent June and WTI May +8-9% to ~$109; UST10 +4bp to 4.36%, Bund 10Y +6bp to 3.05%; DXY +0.7% to 100.2, USD/JPY 159.7. Rate markets again fully price two BoE hikes by end-2026 and almost three ECB hikes; the implied probability of a Fed cut by year-end fell to 10% from 20%. ECB's Panetta: even if fighting stops quickly, the return to normal Gulf output will be slow.

US data 2 Apr: initial jobless claims 202k (212k expected), continuing claims 1.841m; trade deficit $57.3bn in February ($59.2bn expected; exports a record $314.8bn); Challenger announced job cuts 60,620 in March.

Logan (Dallas Fed, 2 Apr) supports holding rates; the labour market has stabilised since H2 2025. IMF Article IV on the US: limited room for cuts in 2026 - staff see perhaps one cut by end-2026, with oil and commodity prices lifting inflation expectations.

2 Apr European close: Brent ~$110 (+7%), WTI up to +12%; UST10 4.30% (-1bp, after +4-5bp), Bund 10Y ~3.0% (+1bp after +6bp); DXY 99.9, USD/JPY 159.4; ECB fix EUR/USD 1.1525. Late New York: Brent June $108.40 (+7.2%), WTI $111.47 (+11.3%); TE: Brent high $109.44. Markets shut on Good Friday 3 Apr (US bonds early close).

Physical oil: Dated (spot North Sea) Brent topped $140/bbl (S&P Global $141.37), the highest since 2008, from just under $128 a day earlier, while futures stayed below that level; NW Europe jet fuel (>$1,900/t) and diesel (>$1,600/t) hit record highs and diesel briefly topped $200/bbl.

2 Apr: a UK-hosted call of 40+ countries demanded Iran reopen Hormuz immediately and unconditionally; Kallas wants the EU Aspides naval mission extended; Macron called a military reopening unrealistic; Iran's deputy FM said Tehran is studying transit fees. Late in the day stocks recovered on reports that Oman and Iran are drafting a protocol to monitor transit through the strait.

S&P Global Ratings (PAP 2 Apr): in its base case with oil averaging $80/bbl in 2026, the negative effects of the shock on CEE and Turkish sovereign ratings will be manageable. Czechia's government will regulate fuel from 8 Apr (max margin CZK2.5/l, diesel excise -CZK2.35/l); Orban said Hungary will keep its fuel price cap for Hungarians despite a Commission demand to drop it.

Fed speakers 2-3 Apr: Williams (FOX): the oil spike could spread to many prices over months, policy is well placed but has limits against oil shocks; Goolsbee: the oil shock comes at an 'inopportune time' with tariff inflation not yet faded and could lift 12-month inflation expectations; Daly (after payrolls): zero or negative job growth need not mean weakness - watch the unemployment rate.

JGB yields at records (PAP, 3 Apr): 2Y 1.391%, the highest since 1995, and 10Y 2.399%, the highest since 1999. Oil had jumped on Thursday: WTI +~12% to $112.06, Brent +~8% to $109.24; markets closed for Good Friday.

US March payrolls +178k (60-65k expected; February revised to -133k from -92k), the strongest since Dec 2024; unemployment rate 4.3% (4.4% expected and prior); average hourly earnings +0.2% m/m (0.3% expected); participation 61.9%. Treasuries fell, 2Y leading (+3-5bp).
US S&P Global PMIs final (3 Apr): services 49.8 (flash 51.1; first contraction in over three years), composite 50.3 (flash 51.4; February 51.9); input-cost inflation at its highest this year.

US tariffs: Trump signed an order imposing 100% tariffs on some pharmaceuticals (20% for firms committing to US production; exemption for those that also sign a lower-price deal) (PAP digest 3 Apr, 'on Thursday').

PAP digest 3 Apr: Trump threatened to destroy Iranian power plants and more bridges (three bridges hit overnight, he told Time) and urged Tehran's new leaders to act fast; the French CMA CGM Kribi became the first Western vessel to transit Hormuz since 28 Feb (Bloomberg); CNN: about half of Iran's ballistic-missile launchers remain intact.

PAP digest 3 Apr: the World Bank's energy price index rose 41.6% in March (gas and oil in Europe); the FAO food price index rose to 128.5 in March (125.5); EU energy commissioner Jorgensen (FT): energy prices will stay higher 'for a very long time', and the EU is considering all options including fuel rationing and further emergency stock releases.
The Senate Banking Committee scheduled a 16 Apr hearing on Warsh's nomination as Fed chair (CNBC, 4 Apr); Senator Tillis says he will not vote to confirm until the DOJ probe of Powell is concluded.

4-5 Apr: Trump issued another 48-hour ultimatum ('hell will come down on them'), then declared Tuesday 'Power Plant Day and Bridge Day' in Iran and moved the deadline to Tue 7 Apr 20:00 ET (02:00 Warsaw on 8 Apr); he said he believes a deal could be reached by Monday. Iran's military rejected the ultimatum; Iran's parliament speaker threatened Bab el-Mandeb shipping.

IEA's Birol (5 Apr): if Hormuz does not reopen, crude and product losses in April will be double March's; 72 regional energy assets are damaged, a third severely or very severely; normalisation will take a long time even if the war ends; Saudi Arabia has rerouted over two-thirds of its exports via the Red Sea pipeline.

Iran shot down a US F-15E over Iran on Fri 3 Apr (a US A-10 was also lost that day, PAP); Trump said on 5 Apr that both crew members had been rescued in the 'most daring' search-and-rescue operation, while Iranian media claimed more US aircraft were downed during the rescue.

Hungary/Serbia (5 Apr): Serbian authorities found a high-power explosive device near the Balkan Stream pipeline carrying Russian gas to Hungary; Orban ordered the army to protect TurkStream; Kyiv denied involvement. Hungary votes on Sun 12 Apr; polls show Tisza ahead.

OPEC+ (Sun 5 Apr) will raise output quotas by 206k b/d from May - under 2% of the supply disrupted by the Hormuz closure, but a signal of readiness to raise output once the strait reopens (Reuters via PAP week-ahead); Gulf officials say restoring production would take months even after a reopening.

PAP week-ahead (6 Apr): the FOMC minutes (Wed 8 Apr, 20:00), February PCE (Thu) and March CPI (Fri) are due; the Fed held at 3.50-3.75% on 17-18 Mar with Miran dissenting for a cut; Powell said last week the Fed can wait and see how the war affects the economy and typically looks through supply shocks; PAP gives the next FOMC as 27-28 Apr.

PAP table of 6 Apr (Easter Monday): European rows are the 2 Apr closes (stamped 3 Apr): Bund 2.99%, OAT 3.68%, BTP 3.85%, Bonos 3.47%, gilt 4.83% -> OAT-Bund 69bp, BTP-Bund 86bp, Spain 48bp; Schatz 2.62%, gilt 2Y 4.32%; CZ10 4.90%, HU10 6.94%. Live 06:27: UST10 4.35%, UST2 3.85% (post-payrolls), JGB10 2.42%.
ISM services 54.0 in March (54.8-55 expected; February 56.1): business activity 53.9, employment 45.2 (first fall in four months), prices paid 70.7 (highest since October 2022).
Hassett (6 Apr): Trump sees the oil price rise as temporary and the Fed is expected to cut after Warsh takes office.

6 Apr (Europe closed for Easter Monday): UST10 4.33-4.36%, 2s10s +48-49bp; DXY ~100.0, EUR/USD 1.1539; Brent June $108.6-109.9; gold $4,683-4,716. Saudi Arabia raised its May OSP to a record premium of $19.50 (Odaily). JPMorgan's Dimon warned the war could push inflation and rates above market expectations.

6 Apr: mediators pushed for a 45-day ceasefire (Axios) and a Pakistani plan was sent to both sides; Trump rejected a 45-day truce (CNN); Iran replied via Pakistan with a 10-point response rejecting a temporary ceasefire and demanding a permanent end to the war; Trump called it 'an important step, but not enough', ruled out extending Tuesday's deadline and said all Iranian power plants and bridges could be destroyed 'within four hours'.

PAP table of 7 Apr: European rows still show the 2 Apr closes (stamped 3 Apr; markets shut 3 and 6 Apr): Bund 2.99%, BTP-Bund 86bp, OAT-Bund 69bp, gilt 4.83%. Live 06:31: UST10 4.34%, UST2 3.86%, JGB10 2.42%.

Hammack (Cleveland Fed, AP interview via PAP): a rate hike could be warranted if inflation stays stuck above 2%; she prefers holding rates steady for 'quite a long time' and sees scenarios requiring moves in either direction (labour-market deterioration or persistent inflation).

Czech flash CPI for March: 1.9% y/y (2.0% expected; February 1.4%), a three-month high, with services 4.7% and energy -1.7% (-7.8%). Czech retail sales +4.1% y/y in February (3.8% expected); the February trade surplus narrowed to CZK19.3bn (27.7bn expected).

ECB's Wunsch (WSJ interview, Mon 6 Apr; via TE 7 Apr) said the ECB may need to raise rates several times, starting as early as this month, if the energy fallout from the war persists. Markets are back to pricing three 25bp ECB hikes in 2026 (PAP 09:28; TE). Bund 10Y rose toward 3.1% after the Easter break.

Final March services PMIs: euro area 50.2 (flash 50.1; 10-month low; new business fell at the fastest pace in 16 months), euro-area composite 50.7 (flash 50.5; February 51.9; weakest since June 2025), Germany services 50.9 (flash 51.2), France composite revised up; UK services 50.5 (flash 51.2), UK composite 50.3 (flash 51.0; six-month low). Input costs rose at the fastest pace since 2023 in several countries. Sentix investor confidence fell to -19.2 in April (-8.0 expected; -3.1 in March).
TE (7 Apr): markets 'firmly' price two BoE hikes in 2026; gilt 10Y up to 4.85%, near the end-March multi-year highs; sterling just above $1.32.

The National Bank of Romania held its policy rate at 6.50% (lending facility 7.50%, deposit 5.50%) on 7 Apr; it expects inflation (9.31% in February; adjusted core 8.3%) to rise through June on oil and gas prices before dropping sharply in Q3; Q4 2025 GDP -1.9% q/q.

Williams (NY Fed, 7 Apr): the war will lift headline inflation (around 2.75% including energy) while core is little changed and should decline later this year; policy is in a good place to wait and see and can be adjusted if needed; 2026 GDP growth 2-2.5%; uncertainty over Warsh's confirmation is not a problem - Powell keeps chairing the FOMC until a successor is confirmed.
New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations: median one-year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 3.4% in March (3.0% in February; 3.5% expected), the highest this year.

OPEC's March crude output plunged by 7.56m b/d (~25%) to 22m b/d, the largest monthly drop in decades (survey via Odaily); the EIA STEO raised its 2026 Brent forecast to $96 (from $78.84) and 2027 to $76.09; WTI 2026 $87.41.

7 Apr European close: Brent June ~$110.1 (+0.3%), WTI $115.6 (+2.8%); EUR/USD 1.1574 (ECB fix 1.1557), USD/JPY 159.9; TTF +4% to EUR52.3/MWh (TE); gold fell below $4,610 after reports that Iran shut communication channels with the US. UST10 4.35% in the morning. Late New York: Brent June ~$105-106 (-3%) on hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough before the deadline.

7 Apr, before the deadline (Tue 20:00 ET = 02:00 Warsaw on 8 Apr): Iran rejected a temporary truce and set preconditions for 'permanent peace' (Reuters); Trump: 'a whole civilization will die tonight' but the threat could change if talks progress; Vance: the war will end soon; Iran was reported to have cut diplomatic channels, then that they remain open; sources reported progress in the last 24 hours (18:37). Kharg Island was struck; Israel hit Iranian railways and bridges; China and Russia vetoed Bahrain's UN Security Council resolution on protecting Hormuz shipping.

Hungary election run-up: US Vice President Vance, visiting Budapest on 7 Apr, said 'Brussels bureaucrats' tried to destroy Hungary's economy because they hate Orban; Trump again urged Hungarians to back Orban. Opposition Tisza led recent polls.

Vice Chair Jefferson (Detroit, 17:50 ET): downside risks to employment and upside risks to inflation; after 175bp of cuts the rate is 'broadly in the range of neutral' and well positioned to respond to a range of outcomes; February PCE estimated at 2.8% and core 3.0%; elevated energy prices will show up in coming inflation readings; Q1 payrolls averaged ~70k a month, likely within break-even.

Ceasefire: at 00:36 Warsaw on 8 Apr (less than two hours before his deadline) Trump said he agreed to Pakistan's proposal for a two-week, 'double-sided' suspension of strikes on Iran, conditional on Iran's complete, immediate and safe reopening of Hormuz; Iran accepted and said safe passage is possible 'in coordination with Iran's armed forces'; the truce took effect at 03:30 Iran time; the White House said Israel also agreed. Trump called Iran's 10-point plan a 'workable basis' for talks and said most points are agreed.

10Y closes 7 Apr (pre-ceasefire): Bund 3.08% (+9bp vs 2 Apr), OAT 3.78%, BTP 3.97%, Bonos 3.57%, gilt 4.90% -> OAT-Bund 70bp, BTP-Bund 89bp, Spain 49bp; Schatz 2.72%, gilt 2Y 4.41%; CZ10 4.97%, HU10 6.90%. Live 06:32 (post-ceasefire): UST10 4.24% (4.29 prior), UST2 3.72% (3.79), JGB10 2.37%.

Hungarian CPI rose to 1.8% y/y in March from a nine-year low of 1.4% (m/m +0.4%, the most since July), while core inflation slowed to 1.9% (2.1%), the lowest since September 2018. Industrial output -1.5% y/y in February; retail sales +3.8% y/y.
TE (8 Apr): traders now price just one BoE hike in 2026, nearly 30bp less than at Tuesday's close; the gilt 10Y fell ~20bp to 4.65%; sterling +1% to ~$1.34 (four-week high).

PAP 8 Apr 09:38: traders aggressively cut ECB hike bets for 2026 to 51bp from 80bp on Tuesday; the odds of a 25bp hike in April fell to 40% from over 70%. Commerzbank's Rieger: if the ceasefire is extended, an April (or later) ECB hike becomes unlikely. TE: one hike removed - two now priced for 2026.

Euro-area data 8 Apr: retail sales -0.2% m/m in February (as expected); PPI -0.7% m/m and -3.0% y/y in February (in line); construction PMI 44.6 in March (46.0); German factory orders +0.9% m/m in February.
TE (8 Apr): with energy prices falling, markets expect the Fed to keep rates unchanged this year, reversing earlier concerns that rising inflation could force a hike.

Trump (8 Apr; Odaily/PAP): any country supplying weapons to Iran will face an immediate 50% tariff on goods sold to the US; talks will cover ending uranium enrichment and sanctions relief; the US will help restore traffic through Hormuz; he floated a 'joint venture' with Iran on the strait (ABC). US officials insist Iran must remove nuclear material and stop enrichment.

8 Apr ceasefire rally: Brent June -13% to $95.11 at 18:20 (intraday ~$91.7; late New York $94.75, the steepest one-day drop since 2020) and WTI -16% (settled $94.41, the largest daily fall since April 2020); TTF -15% to EUR45.3/MWh (five-week low); DXY -1.0% to 98.82, EUR/USD 1.1688 (ECB fix 1.1706), USD/JPY 158.3; Bund 10Y -14bp to 2.94%; UST10 4.27% (-2bp, 4.23% earlier); gold +2.1% to $4,760; Dow +2.85%, its best day since April 2025.

FOMC minutes (17-18 Mar), released 20:00 Warsaw: almost all participants backed the hold; several pushed back the likely timing of cuts given recent inflation; 'some' (vs 'several' in January) saw a strong case for two-sided guidance in the statement, reflecting that hikes could be appropriate if inflation stays above target; the vast majority judged upside inflation and downside employment risks elevated, most saying they had risen with the Middle East conflict; most worried a prolonged conflict could weaken the labour market and justify further cuts, while many saw a risk of oil-driven inflation persisting that could require hikes.

Truce frictions on 8 Apr: Trump and Netanyahu said Lebanon/Hezbollah is not covered; Israel kept striking Lebanon; Iranian media said tanker traffic through Hormuz was halted after Israeli attacks (Fars) and the navy said ships still need permission; Reuters sources said the strait remained closed; the UAE said it was targeted by 17 missiles and 25 drones despite the truce, and a Saudi oil pipeline to the Red Sea was hit by drones (Bloomberg); an Iranian official said a limited reopening on Tehran's terms is possible Thu/Fri. The White House said Vance will lead US talks with Iran in Islamabad on Saturday 11 Apr.

IEA's Birol (8 Apr): if Hormuz is not fully reopened, jet-fuel shortages could disrupt European air traffic from mid-May; the EU oil coordination group sees no urgent April supply risk. Qatar began work to restore LNG plant output; Maersk is not yet resuming Hormuz routes; ING: oil will fall only gradually and not quickly return to pre-war levels.
Macron (8 Apr): about 15 countries plan to join a mission to restore shipping through Hormuz. The WSJ reported late on 8 Apr that Trump is considering withdrawing US troops from some NATO allies.

Timiraos (WSJ, 8 Apr evening): the ceasefire may swap one problem for another for the Fed - energy-price volatility enough to keep inflation elevated but not to crush demand, prolonging the hold; the minutes show the war is not the main reason for reluctance to cut. Daly (SF Fed): US fundamentals remain in good shape.

10Y closes 8 Apr (ceasefire day): Bund 2.94% (-14bp), OAT 3.58%, BTP 3.71% (-26bp), Bonos 3.38%, gilt 4.71% -> OAT-Bund 64bp, BTP-Bund 77bp, Spain 44bp; Schatz 2.49% (-23bp), gilt 2Y 4.17% (-24bp); CZ2 4.00% (-24bp), CZ10 4.75%, HU10 6.72%. Live 06:33: UST10 4.29%, UST2 3.79%, JGB10 2.40%.
German data 9 Apr: exports +3.6% m/m in February (+1.3% expected); industrial production -0.3% m/m (+0.7% expected).
Czech industrial output +1.3% y/y in February (1.5% expected), construction +4.1% y/y; CNB reserves fell to $179bn in March (gold valuation). Romania Q4 GDP final +0.2% y/y, weakest since 2021.
TE (9 Apr): Bund 10Y rebounded to ~2.98% as oil rose on ceasefire doubts; traders price at least two ECB hikes by end-2026. BoE: at least one hike by end-2026 priced; gilt 10Y back to 4.7%.

9 Apr (Odaily/PAP): on Iran's planned transit fees the Commission said the law of the sea allows no fees (Iran reportedly wants $1/bbl from tankers); US media said the administration may soon ease sanctions on Iranian oil to stabilise supply; Trump pressed NATO allies to help secure Hormuz and, per Reuters, is discussing withdrawing some US troops from Europe; Merz said oil may rise further and Germany will support a maritime mission.

Hassett (9 Apr): Warsh will take over as Fed chair in May as planned and Powell is not expected to remain on the Board; Fed balance-sheet reduction should be gradual; oil prices will fall relatively quickly once Hormuz opens.

US data 9 Apr: February PCE prices +0.4% m/m, 2.8% y/y (as expected), core +0.4% m/m and 3.0% y/y; personal income -0.1% m/m (+0.3% expected), spending +0.5%; Q4 GDP (third estimate) cut to +0.5% annualised (0.7%); initial claims 219k (210-212k expected), continuing claims 1.794m (lowest in nearly two years). Market reaction muted.
PAP 9 Apr (pre-data): money markets priced ~30% odds of a 25bp Fed cut by end-2026, down from 56% a day earlier.

IMF's Georgieva (9 Apr): the IMF will lower its global growth forecast because of the war even in the most optimistic scenario (infrastructure damage, supply disruptions, lost confidence); short-term inflation expectations have risen but long-term ones are unchanged; short-term IMF support needs may rise to $20-50bn.

9 Apr European close: Bund 10Y 2.99% (+5bp); UST10 4.28% (-2bp), 2s10s +51bp; DXY 98.79, EUR/USD 1.1701 (ECB fix 1.1685), USD/JPY 158.9; Brent June $96.86 (+2.3%; TE: above $99 intraday), WTI ~$100 (+5.9%); TTF EUR44.69 (-1.5%); gold $4,818 (+0.9%), silver $75.9.

9 Apr, a fragile truce (PAP digest; Odaily): Hezbollah resumed fire after Israel's heaviest strikes on Lebanon (at least 254 civilians killed on 8 Apr) and Iranian media said Hormuz was 'completely closed'; Iran's deputy FM then said it is open but passage requires coordination; a senior source said at most 15 ships a day will be allowed during the truce and demanded that US-held assets be unfrozen within two weeks; Iran published a map of mines in the strait. Pezeshkian said Israeli attacks make talks pointless; Trump asked Netanyahu to scale back strikes, and Netanyahu agreed to direct talks with Lebanon. Mojtaba Khamenei: Iran does not seek war but will not give up its rights.
Russia announced an Orthodox Easter truce in Ukraine from 11 Apr 15:00 (Warsaw) to the end of 12 Apr; Zelensky confirmed it. Putin envoy Dmitriev is in the US for talks with the administration.

PAP table of 10 Apr (no date stamps; EU rows = 9 Apr closes): Bund 2.99%, OAT 3.61%, BTP 3.74%, Bonos 3.43%, gilt 4.75% -> OAT-Bund 62bp, BTP-Bund 75bp, Spain 44bp; Schatz 2.52%, gilt 2Y 4.18%; CZ2 4.05%, CZ10 4.81%, HU10 6.65%. UST10 4.30%, UST2 3.79%, JGB10 2.43%.
German final March CPI 2.7% y/y (HICP 2.8%), confirming the flash and the highest since January 2024; energy +7.2% y/y (fuel +20%, heating oil +44%).

TE (10 Apr): traders price at least two ECB hikes by end-2026 with ~30% odds of a third; the Bund 10Y is back above 3%, near the 15-year high of 3.13% set in late March; BoE: at least one hike priced by end-2026. EUR/USD at a six-week high near $1.172.
Czech registered unemployment fell to 5.0% in March (5.1% expected; 5.2% in February).

Daly (SF Fed, 10 Apr): she sees a hike as less likely than a cut or a hold; a cut is 'not impossible' if the conflict is resolved quickly and oil falls, but if inflation stays above expectations the Fed will wait until confident; if the ceasefire holds, the CPI print becomes irrelevant.
CME FedWatch 10 Apr before CPI: April hold 98.4%, hike 1.6%; by June: cut 1.5%, hold 96.8%, hike 1.7% - unchanged after the CPI release.

US March CPI +0.9% m/m (as expected; largest since 2022) and 3.3% y/y (3.3-3.4% expected; 2.4% in February), the highest since May 2024; energy +10.9% m/m (12.5% y/y, gasoline +18.9% y/y) - gasoline accounts for ~3/4 of the rise; core +0.2% m/m (0.3% expected) and 2.6% y/y (2.7% expected). Timiraos: core 0.196%, slightly soft, but one month does not change the Fed's assessment.

After CPI (Jin10/Reuters via Odaily): bets on one Fed cut this year increased somewhat, but market pricing still points to the Fed holding through 2026; Goldman: the Fed has room for patience. Hassett: the Fed still has room to cut; Hormuz could open within two months.

10 Apr (PAP): Brent June ~$95.4-96.9 during the day (09:03: down 11% on the week), WTI ~$97.5-99; DXY ~98.7-98.8, EUR/USD 1.1722 (ECB fix 1.1711), USD/JPY 159.1-159.3; Bund 10Y 3.03% (+4bp, 14:49); UST10 4.29%; gold $4,788. Wall Street fell on Friday but some indices had their best week since November; late New York Brent ~$94.5.

UMich preliminary April: sentiment collapsed to a record-low 47.6 (51.5-52 expected; 55.3 in March), with 98% of interviews before the ceasefire; one-year inflation expectations jumped to 4.8% (3.8%; 4.2-4.3% expected), long-run 3.4% (3.2%). February durable goods final -1.3% m/m.

10 Apr, ahead of talks (Odaily/PAP): Iran's deputy FM said the parties agreed Iran's 10-point plan will be the basis of negotiations; Vance's delegation left for Pakistan; Trump: Iran has 'no cards' except short-term extortion via waterways and the US is ready militarily if talks fail, with the outcome clear within 24 hours; Iran signalled it would seek a permanent ban on US/Israel-linked tankers; over 600 ships including 325 tankers remain trapped around Hormuz (Gulf News); Japan will release 20 days of oil reserves in May.
The Commission sees no need to trigger the general escape clause of EU fiscal rules for the war-related energy crisis (10 Apr).

11 Apr: US (Vance) and Iranian (Ghalibaf) delegations met face to face in Islamabad with Pakistan; two US destroyers transited Hormuz to prepare mine-clearing (CENTCOM) and Trump said the US is 'clearing' the strait; Iran's stated red lines: Hormuz control, war reparations, unfrozen assets and a region-wide ceasefire; reports that the US agreed to unfreeze assets were denied by the White House.

12 Apr (02:58-04:00 Warsaw): the Islamabad talks ended after ~21 hours without agreement; Vance: Iran chose not to accept US terms, the US made a final offer; Iran's FM spokesman: differences on two or three important issues (nuclear programme, Hormuz). Later on 12 Apr Trump (Fox) said Iran will return to talks but ordered the US Navy to blockade ships entering or leaving Hormuz, seize vessels that paid Iranian transit fees and clear mines; he conceded oil prices could rise; the UK and others would send minesweepers; NATO should be 'rethought' (PAP weekend digest 20:48).

Hungary election (Sun 12 Apr): with 15% of list votes counted Peter Magyar's opposition Tisza had 47.8% vs Fidesz-KDNP 43.6%; Magyar called for calm and was cautiously optimistic, while Orban's chief of staff said Fidesz hoped for a majority (PAP weekend digest).
Sunday-night open (13 Apr 00:09): Brent futures jumped ~8% to ~$103 after Trump announced the Hormuz blockade following the failed talks (TE); TTF was expected to jump.

US blockade: CENTCOM blockades all vessels entering or leaving Iranian ports and coastal areas from 10:00 ET (16:00 Warsaw) on 13 Apr, without impeding transit to non-Iranian ports; over 15 warships are involved; Trump said US forces will attack Iranian ships approaching them and that Iran called wanting a deal. Iran called it 'piracy' and warned no port in the region would be safe; Hormuz traffic halted again; the UK will not join the blockade (Starmer) and will co-host with France a conference on a Hormuz shipping mission; the WSJ said Trump also weighs limited strikes.

Hungarian assets rallied on Tisza's two-thirds win: the forint strengthened more than 1% to ~315 per dollar, the strongest since February 2022 (and a four-year high vs the euro, PAP); the Budapest index hit a record; the HU10Y fell to 6.31% (TE 13:58), the lowest since November 2024 (-51bp in four weeks). Markets expect around EUR17bn of frozen EU grants to be unlocked. Von der Leyen urged using the momentum to replace unanimity with QMV in EU foreign policy.

Hungary: Orban conceded defeat on Sunday night; projections with ~98-99% counted give Tisza 138 of 199 seats, a two-thirds constitutional majority, Fidesz-KDNP 55 and Mi Hazank 6-7 (NVI via PAP/TE). Capital Economics: investors will welcome the clear result; a turning point if Tisza quickly restores EU relations, unlocks funds and signals medium-term fiscal stability.

PAP week-ahead (13 Apr): IMF/World Bank spring meetings run 13-18 Apr (IMF WEO on Tuesday; G20 finance ministers on Thursday); Fed Beige Book on Wednesday; the ECB's account of its March meeting is due (16 Apr); speakers include Lagarde (14 Apr 23:00), Bailey (14-15 Apr), Goolsbee, Barr, Barkin, Collins, Paulson (14 Apr), Bowman (15 Apr) and Williams (16 Apr).

10Y closes 10 Apr: Bund 3.06%, OAT 3.71%, BTP 3.84%, Bonos 3.52%, gilt 4.84% -> OAT-Bund 65bp, BTP-Bund 78bp, Spain 46bp; Schatz 2.60%, gilt 2Y 4.26%; CZ2 4.03%, CZ10 4.77%, HU10 6.55%. Live 06:31: UST10 4.34%, UST2 3.83%, JGB10 2.47%.
TE (13 Apr): traders price nearly two BoE hikes by end-2026, up from one last week; gilt 10Y up to 4.8%.
TE (13 Apr): with Brent back near $102, traders price nearly three ECB hikes by year-end, up from two last week (TE's Bund piece: at least two); Bund 10Y 3.06%, near its 15-year high of 3.13%.
Czech February current-account surplus narrowed to CZK17.4bn (CZK34.2bn expected; CZK49.7bn a year earlier).
US existing home sales fell 3.6% m/m to 3.98m annualised in March (4.05-4.06m expected), a nine-month low.

13 Apr European close: Brent June $101.84 (+7%), WTI $102.7 (+6.3%); TTF +5.9% to EUR46.2/MWh; Bund 10Y 3.09% (+3bp); UST10 4.33% (+1bp); DXY 98.79 (+0.15%; 99.0 in the morning), EUR/USD 1.1709 (ECB fix 1.1684), USD/JPY 159.7; gold $4,735 (-1.1%), silver $74.2. TE: Brent later ~$98 (+2.9%). The S&P 500 closed having recovered all its losses since the war began.

Axios (13 Apr): in Islamabad the US demanded a 20-year suspension of uranium enrichment and removal of highly enriched uranium; Iran offered a single-digit number of years. Iran's FM said the sides were 'one step away' from a deal; Pakistan, Egypt and Turkey continue mediation and Pakistan says the ceasefire remains in effect; Netanyahu: the ceasefire with Iran may end soon.

14 Apr: AP said US-Iran talks may resume on Thursday; Pakistan invited both sides back to Islamabad and Trump said talks could take place within two days; Iran's formal reply offered to halt enrichment for up to five years, which the US rejected (it asked for 20 years and removal of enriched uranium); Bloomberg: Iran is considering briefly pausing its own Hormuz shipping to avoid testing the blockade; CENTCOM said no ship breached the blockade in its first 24 hours; a US official said there is no full blockade of Hormuz; Saudi Arabia urged the US to lift it; China warned of countermeasures if the US imposes Iran-related tariffs on it.

10Y closes 13 Apr (blockade day): Bund 3.09%, OAT 3.75%, BTP 3.89%, Bonos 3.55%, gilt 4.87% -> OAT-Bund 66bp, BTP-Bund 80bp, Spain 46bp; Schatz 2.65%, gilt 2Y 4.32%; CZ2 3.99%, CZ10 4.79%, HU10 6.23% (-32bp, post-election). Live 06:32: UST10 4.28%, UST2 3.77%, JGB10 2.43%.
Romanian CPI rose to 9.9% y/y in March (10.4% expected; 9.3% in February), a six-month high, with fuel +12.9% y/y; m/m +0.78%.
Czech final March CPI confirmed at 1.9% y/y (1.4% in February); fuel prices swung to +13.1% y/y from -8.4%.

US March PPI +0.5% m/m (1.1% expected) and 4.0% y/y (4.6% expected; February 3.4%); core +0.1% m/m (0.4-0.5% expected) and 3.8% y/y (4.1%); goods +1.6% (energy +8.5%), services flat (trade margins fell). NFIB small-business optimism fell to 95.8 in March (98.8).

IMF World Economic Outlook (14 Apr): 2026 world growth cut by 0.2pp to 3.1%; if the conflict and high oil prices persist, growth could fall to 2.5% or lower (Xinhua via Odaily). IMF sees Poland at 3.3% (2026) and 2.4% (2027), CPI 3.3% in both years (PAP).
TE (14 Apr): markets price a nearly 30% chance of a Fed cut this year; the dollar fell to a one-month low and gold rose as oil retreated on hopes of renewed US-Iran talks.

Bessent (14 Apr): the Fed can wait and observe before cutting and should wait until Warsh is in place; he is confident core inflation will keep falling; the 10% Section 122 tariff is in place and Trump has not decided whether to raise it to 15%. Hassett: the Fed still has room to cut. Senate Banking chair Scott: Warsh's confirmation hearing will be held next week (21 Apr; Fox: hurdles to his confirmation cleared).

Lagarde (Bloomberg TV, 14 Apr): the euro-area economy is somewhere between the ECB's baseline for the Iran war and the less favourable scenario. TE: traders price at least two ECB hikes by end-2026; BoE nearly two hikes by year-end; gilt 10Y toward 4.7%.

14 Apr European close: Brent June $95.95 (-3.5%; TE late ~$95, -4%), WTI $93.30 (-5.8%); Bund 10Y 3.02% (-7bp); UST10 4.27% (-2bp), 2s10s +51bp; DXY 98.0 (-0.3%), EUR/USD 1.1789 (ECB fix 1.1793; above 1.18 intraday, erasing its war losses), GBP ~$1.36 (highest since mid-February), USD/JPY 158.85; gold $4,835 (+1.4%), silver $79.4.

IEA monthly report (14 Apr): global oil demand will fall in 2026 for the first time since 2020 as war-driven prices hit GDP; Birol: current prices do not reflect the situation and may still rise. US Energy Secretary Wright: prices stay high until significant traffic resumes through Hormuz.

Trade (14 Apr): the EU agreed (Parliament-Council deal) to tighten its steel safeguard, doubling tariffs and nearly halving tariff-free import quotas; the Commission will assess euro-convergence of non-euro members incl. Hungary this summer (Magyar wants the euro).

Goldman Sachs: hike likelihood this year remains low despite volatile fed-funds pricing (analyst view, not pricing).
CME FedWatch 1 Apr (pre-ADP): April hold 99.5%, hike 0.5%; by June cut 9.4%, hold 90.1%, hike 0.5%.

CME FedWatch 10 Apr (pre-CPI): April hold 98.4%, hike 1.6%; by June cut 1.5%, hold 96.8%, hike 1.7%.
Jin10 10 Apr (post-CPI): bets on one Fed cut this year increased; Reuters: pricing still centred on no change through 2026.
CME FedWatch 10 Apr 15:19 (post-CPI): April hold 98.4%, unchanged from before the release.
TE 14 Apr: markets price a nearly 30% chance of a Fed cut this year as oil eased and the dollar hit a one-month low.

digest.2026-04-01: Euro-area flash HICP jumped to 2.5% in March (2.6% expected; core 2.3%); markets price at least two ECB hikes in 2026 (~50% for April) and two BoE hikes. The WSJ said Trump is ready to end the war even with Hormuz largely shut. Brent rose a record ~50% in March (expiring May contract ~$119); the Bund 10Y is ~3.0% after its biggest monthly rise since 2022; UST10 4.33%.
digest.2026-04-02: Trump said the US could leave Iran within two-three weeks and core bonds rallied (UST10 4.28-4.30%, Bund 10Y 2.95-2.99%, gilt 4.82%); Brent June briefly fell below $100 and closed near $101. ECB pricing eased to two 2026 hikes and BoE to fewer than two. US ISM manufacturing 52.7 with prices paid at 78.3; FedWatch ~99.5% for an April hold.
digest.2026-04-07: Trump's address promised two-three more weeks of heavy strikes and Brent jumped ~8% to ~$109 (Dated Brent above $140); the Bund 10Y was back near 3% and markets again priced almost three ECB and two BoE hikes. US payrolls +178k (60k expected) with unemployment at 4.3% left ~1bp of 2026 Fed easing priced. Trump set an 8 Apr 02:00 (Warsaw) deadline, threatening Iran's power plants.
digest.2026-04-08: Ahead of Trump's deadline Iran rejected a temporary truce; Brent held ~$110 before sliding to ~$105 late on deal hopes. Markets priced three ECB hikes and Wunsch said hikes could start in April; two BoE hikes priced. Euro-area composite PMI 50.7, Sentix -19.2; Czech March CPI 1.9%; NBR held at 6.50%. Williams and Jefferson: policy well positioned, risks on both sides.
digest.2026-04-09: A two-week US-Iran ceasefire (announced 00:36) sent Brent down ~13% to ~$95 and TTF 15% to EUR45; the Bund 10Y fell 14bp to 2.94% and gilts ~20bp. ECB hike pricing dropped to ~51bp from 80bp (April odds 40%), BoE to one hike. FOMC minutes: more officials want two-sided guidance. The truce looked fragile as Israel kept striking Lebanon and Hormuz stayed largely shut.
digest.2026-04-10: The truce wobbled - Iran capped Hormuz transits (~15 ships a day) over Israeli strikes on Lebanon - and Brent rebounded to ~$97-99. The Bund 10Y was back at 2.99% with at least two 2026 ECB hikes priced. US February core PCE 3.0%, Q4 GDP 0.5%; odds of a 2026 Fed cut fell to ~30% from 56%. Hassett: Warsh takes over in May. The IMF will cut its world growth forecast.
digest.2026-04-13: US March CPI 3.3% (core 2.6%, slightly soft) and UMich 1Y inflation expectations jumped to 4.8%; FedWatch still ~98% for an April hold; ECB priced for two hikes (30% for a third). Brent ~$95, down ~11% on the week. The Islamabad talks ended on 12 Apr without a deal and Trump ordered a naval blockade of Hormuz; early Hungarian returns put Tisza ahead of Fidesz.
digest.2026-04-14: The US blockade of Iranian ports began and Brent jumped back to ~$102 (TTF +6%), lifting ECB pricing to nearly three hikes and BoE to nearly two; Bund 10Y 3.09%, UST10 4.33%. Tisza won a two-thirds majority in Hungary: the forint hit its strongest vs the dollar since 2022 and the HU10Y fell to ~6.3%. Iran said a deal was 'one step away'; the S&P 500 erased its war losses.
digest.2026-04-15: Hopes of a second round of US-Iran talks pushed Brent back to ~$95 and EUR/USD above 1.18 (DXY at a one-month low); the Bund 10Y fell 7bp to 3.02%. US March PPI undershot (4.0% y/y, core +0.1% m/m). The IMF cut 2026 world growth to 3.1% (2.5% if the conflict persists) and the IEA sees oil demand falling this year; ECB still priced for two hikes; Romanian CPI 9.9%.
